text:
KörkortGo · M08-L02 · Check coupling load
Check coupling load
Towball load · A separate force. Towball load (kultryck) is the trailer's downward load at the
coupling, not the trailer's whole loaded weight. With a conventional towball behind the car's
rear axle, excessive downward force acts through a lever arm: it increases rear loading while
reducing the load carried by the front axle. Front unloading does not require the wheels to leave
the road. With less front-tyre loading, available steering grip and response can be impaired.
Official towing guide: front-wheel unloading, page 6
Trafikverket warns that incorrect coupling pressure can lift the car or trailer. Follow the specified
towball, coupling, axle and vehicle limits for the actual combination; there is no universal
number in this lesson. Measure and redistribute the load as instructed before travelling. Total
trailer weight, coupling load and cargo securing are separate checks. Do not cure excessive
downward load by guessing or creating an equally unsuitable load distribution. Trafikverket:
coupling-load caution · Official towing guide: ratings and load distribution
Worked loading decision. Your total trailer weight is within the car's towing limit, but a heavy
object far forward makes the coupling load excessive. The total-weight check has not proved
suitable axle loading. Stop preparation, establish the specified limits and adjust and secure the
load before driving.

M08-L03
Keep the car legally ready
Your goal: Build an ownership checklist for registration, insurance, inspection and vehicle
status.
Requirements. The registered owner of an on-road car must have compulsory motor insurance.
Not using the car, or having a defect or driving prohibition, does not by itself end that obligation;
formal off-road status matters. Compulsory insurance covers specified traffic injuries and
damage to others, not every loss to your own car. Optional cover varies by policy. Compulsory
motor insurance
For an ordinary car or light goods vehicle up to 3,500 kg, the normal inspection sequence is: first
by 36 months after the month of first use, second by 24 months after the first inspection month,
then by 14 months after the preceding inspection month. Check the recorded date and any
special category or exemption for your vehicle. An earlier inspection changes the next
calculation; an old reminder is not proof of the current deadline. Inspection intervals
An on-road registration status, valid insurance and completed inspection answer different
questions. Check the vehicle's status and any prohibition before use, and deal with tax
obligations through the current official service. A car being physically driveable does not
establish legal readiness. On-road and off-road status
Ownership process. Transportstyrelsen currently provides eligible private-person transfers
through Mina sidor; other cases may require the latest registration certificate part 2. The service
has eligibility conditions. Consult the current instructions instead of relying on an old app or a
remembered screen sequence. Part 1 and the vehicle enquiry service provide technical
information; protect ownership documents appropriately. Ownership transfer · Registration
certificate

text:
KörkortGo · M08-L03 · Resolve a missed inspection
Resolve a missed inspection
Inspection deadline · An automatic ban. If the required periodic inspection deadline is missed,
an automatic driving ban (inträtt körförbud) applies. You remain responsible even without a
reminder. Booking a later appointment does not end the ban. The deadline ban lasts until the
inspection has been carried out; follow its result, since defects can bring a new prohibition or a
repair/reinspection requirement. Check the vehicle record before ordinary use.
Transportstyrelsen: missed inspection · Vehicle Regulation, chapter 6 §§15–21
Restricted trips. With an overdue-inspection ban and on-road status (påställd), only the shortest
suitable route to a repair workshop for repair or to an inspection business for inspection is
permitted. If the vehicle is off-road (avställd) and the ban still applies, the exception is the
shortest suitable route to the nearest inspection business. Traffic insurance and other applicable
requirements still matter; the off-road exception requires no unpaid vehicle taxes. It does not
permit errands or commuting. A prohibition issued because the vehicle is dangerously defective
has different conditions: it must be recovered from the place where that prohibition is issued.
Transportstyrelsen: inspection prohibitions · Transportstyrelsen: off-road inspection conditions
Worked deadline. An ordinary light car's recorded inspection deadline is 31 October 2026.
Without the required inspection, the deadline ban starts on 1 November. An appointment on 5
November does not allow normal driving on 2 November. Arrange a permitted inspection trip, or
transport if it cannot be driven safely and lawfully, then follow the inspection result. These dates
illustrate the rule; use the actual vehicle's record. Vehicle Regulation, chapter 6 §§15 and 21
Worked decision. A buyer collects an on-road car but assumes the seller's insurance is enough
for the trip home. The buyer checks the transfer and arranges the required cover from the
applicable ownership date before driving. The sale does not transfer the seller's insurance as
personal cover for the buyer.

text:
KörkortGo · M08-L04
M08-L04
Know what assistance cannot do
Your goal: Explain why safety systems and powertrain differences do not remove your
duties to observe and control.
Trafikverket describes modern protection as including crashworthiness and systems such as
lane assistance and automatic emergency braking. These functions can help, but a good safety
rating is not a promise that any collision can be avoided. Recent official crash testing also shows
the limits of automatic braking in severe truck-trailer collision scenarios. Crash safety ·
Trafikverket: braking and truck-trailer tests
ABS is anti-lock braking. It helps retain the ability to develop steering and braking forces
together, within available friction. Stability control reduces the risk of skid crashes; it does not
create extra road grip or excuse excessive speed. The driver still has to maintain control and an
appropriate speed. VTI friction report, section 4.3 · Trafikverket: tyre and stability advice · Traffic
Regulation, chapter 3 §14
Powertrain awareness. A plug-in hybrid can operate on electricity and with a combustion
engine. That difference matters when interpreting fuel use and emissions: do not assume that
every journey is electrically powered. Transportstyrelsen: plug-in hybrids
For the actual vehicle, establish how it becomes ready to move, how drive and reverse are
selected, how it is secured, and what warnings or assistance limitations need attention. Do not
transfer a universal gear-change, engine-speed, coasting or brake-check recipe between
manual, automatic, hybrid and electric vehicles. Vehicle-specific procedures need the vehicle's
own instructions and practical teaching. The curriculum's role is to help you identify those
questions, not guess their answers.

KörkortGo · M09-L01
M09-L01
Look beyond the exhaust
Your goal: Compare climate, air-quality and noise effects without assuming that a vehicle
has no environmental impact.
Transportstyrelsen distinguishes several effects. Greenhouse-gas emissions relate to the amount
of travel, fuels, energy efficiency and electrification. Air pollution includes exhaust emissions and
wear particles from brakes, tyres and the road. Noise is another effect, with tyre-road noise
becoming important as speed rises. These are different measures: improving one does not prove
that every environmental effect has disappeared. Climate and energy · Air quality · Noise
Learning approach. Ask what a comparison includes. Does an emissions figure describe a test
result, the actual journey or a broader lifecycle? Are you comparing equal distances and
occupancy? If the basis is missing, avoid a confident numerical conclusion. This lesson does not
assign a universal emissions saving to a powertrain or declare a whole journey “zero impact.”
A plug-in hybrid combines electrical and combustion-engine operation. Transportstyrelsen
changed the weighting used for new registrations in 2026 to better reflect the mix of those
modes. The general lesson is to understand what a reported figure represents; it is not a promise
about your next journey's consumption. Transportstyrelsen: plug-in-hybrid weighting

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L01 · Understand emissions
Understand emissions
Emissions explained · Fossil carbon and a cold catalyst. Fossil petrol contains carbon stored for
millions of years. Burning it combines that carbon with oxygen and releases CO₂ into the
atmosphere. The added CO₂ strengthens the natural greenhouse effect and contributes to
warming. Long-stored carbon: Naturvårdsverket · Climate effect: Trafikverket
A conventional petrol car's three-way catalyst reduces carbon monoxide, hydrocarbons and
nitrogen oxides by chemical conversion. It needs sufficient heat to become effective, so it is least
effective just after a cold start. Conversion products include water and CO₂: cleaning up these
pollutants does not capture the fossil carbon or cancel its climate impact. No single warm-up
time applies to every car. Transportstyrelsen: catalyst operation, page 24 · Trafikverket: cold
emission controls
Pollutant comparison. Keep CO distinct from CO₂. The table summarises different mechanisms;
one cleaner exhaust measure cannot stand for all of them.
Substance
Why it matters
CO₂ · carbon dioxide
Added fossil CO₂ strengthens the greenhouse effect.
CO · carbon monoxide
Binds strongly to haemoglobin and interferes with the blood's oxygen transport.
NOx · nitrogen oxides
Can irritate airways, contribute to acidification and, with hydrocarbons and
sunlight, form ground-level ozone.
Traffic particles
Exhaust and wear particles can enter and harm the respiratory system.
Trafikverket: CO, NOx and particle mechanisms · Trafikverket: CO₂ and warming

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L01 · Compare powertrains and washing
Compare powertrains and washing
Powertrain and washing · Check the boundary. A battery-electric car uses only electricity for
propulsion and has no combustion tailpipe exhaust while driving. That does not remove impacts
from vehicle/battery production, raw-material extraction or electricity supply. Tyre and road
wear still matter. A plug-in hybrid combines electric and combustion operation and its traction
battery can be charged externally. A conventional non-plug-in hybrid cannot be charged from an
external electricity supply. Trafikverket: electric cars and hybrid types
Choose a purpose-built automatic or self-service wash that collects and treats its wastewater.
Washing on an ordinary street or driveway can carry oil, metals and cleaning chemicals into
ground or surface water. Treatment reduces the problem but does not remove every pollutant.
Follow the facility's product instructions and local water-protection rules. Göteborg
environmental authority: washing and treatment
Apply the comparison. A catalyst-equipped petrol car still releases fossil CO₂. An electric car
avoids combustion exhaust on that drive, but needs a broader production-and-energy
comparison. For either car, choose washing by how the dirty water is handled, rather than
assuming a mild detergent makes street runoff harmless.
Worked decision. Two vehicles are advertised using different environmental measures. One
figure describes exhaust emissions under a test procedure; another describes noise. The learner
does not rank them as though both figures measure the same thing. They first identify the
question being answered and the information still missing.

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L02
M09-L02
Use energy with foresight
Your goal: Plan anticipatory driving that reduces unnecessary energy use while preserving
safety.
Transportstyrelsen recommends correct tyre pressure, observing speed limits and removing
unused roof racks or roof boxes. Driving technique and environmental awareness are part of
driver education and assessment. Transportstyrelsen: economical driving
Learning approach. Look ahead and respond early to a developing queue rather than
accelerating towards it and then braking sharply. Choose a suitable speed and preserve a gap
that lets you adapt smoothly. This is not an instruction to delay necessary braking: safe control
and traffic duties come first. If you need to stop for a person, do so regardless of what an
efficiency display suggests. Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§2 and 14
Prepare the vehicle for the trip. Check the specified tyre pressure and remove unnecessary
external carrying equipment when it is no longer needed. Combine these habits with realistic
route and timing decisions. Avoid claiming a fixed percentage saving: load, road, weather,
vehicle and technique all affect the outcome.
Vehicle-specific boundary. Gear selection and deceleration strategies vary. Do not use a fixed
engine-speed rule for every car or assume every powertrain cuts fuel or recovers energy in the
same way. Learn the actual vehicle's approved operation with your instructor. This book does
not recommend coasting in neutral or switching the vehicle off while moving.

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L02 · Use energy with control
Use energy with control
Practical energy choices · Prepare and control the car. Use a timer with an installed electric
engine heater so it warms the engine when needed, without running unnecessarily long. Set it
for the intended departure using the equipment instructions and conditions; there is no
universal heating duration. Gagnef municipal energy advice: heater timer
Air conditioning consumes energy, but it can support comfort, alertness and clear windows.
Avoid unnecessary cooling while keeping those safety benefits. Use the car's appropriate
demisting controls; visibility takes priority over a saving. Cooling is not a remedy for sleep
deprivation: stop and rest if drowsy. Revisit M07-L01 for seeing clearly and M07-L03 for attention.
NZ Transport Agency: cooling, alertness and demisting
In a conventional manual car, choose a suitably high gear in which the engine runs smoothly
without labouring. Change down if the load or gradient makes that gear unsuitable. Engine
braking means slowing with the accelerator released while a suitable gear remains engaged; do
not disengage the drive by pressing the clutch or selecting neutral for this technique. Use the
brakes whenever safety requires. Actual engine control varies, so this definition does not
promise zero fuel use or a universal RPM. Official vehicle agency: comfortable gear choice and
in-gear deceleration
Unnecessary carried mass increases the demands on the vehicle. Unload heavy equipment you
no longer need before future journeys, while retaining necessary safety and access equipment.
Removing cargo is a different check from removing a roof box's air resistance. Swedish public
energy advice: minimise weight
Apply before departure. Remove unused heavy equipment, schedule the heater for the trip, and
keep effective demisting. On an uphill section, use the gear the car can comfortably handle; a
high gear that strains the engine is not the intended economical technique.

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L02 · Calculate journey consumption and savings
Calculate journey consumption and
savings
Fuel arithmetic · Understand the unit. A consumption rate of 6.5 litres per 100 km means 6.5
litres for each 100 km under the supplied or measured conditions. A 200 km journey at the same
assumed rate uses twice as much, while 50 km uses half as much. Actual consumption varies
with vehicle, load, road, weather and driving. Transportstyrelsen: economical driving supplies
the driving context; the equations below are editorial arithmetic derived from the unit, not
agency-prescribed formulas.
Journey consumption: journey litres = distance in km × consumption in litres/100 km ÷ 100.
Divide distance by 100 to find the number of 100 km portions, then multiply by the supplied rate.
The kilometres cancel, leaving litres. Retain decimal working and round only the final result at
the precision requested.
Consumption example · 120 km at 6.5 litres/100 km. The journey contains 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2
portions of 100 km. Consumption = 1.2 × 6.5 = 7.8 litres. Do not multiply distance by the rate
without dividing by 100; that would misread the unit.
Savings from a supplied reduction: litres saved = distance in km × reduction in litres/100 km ÷
100. If two consumption rates are supplied, subtract the lower rate from the higher first. Multiply
that difference by the number of 100 km portions. A supplied saving is an exercise assumption,
not a guaranteed benefit of a particular driving technique.
Savings example · A reduction of 1.5 litres/100 km over 300 km. The journey has 300 ÷ 100 = 3
portions. Savings = 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 litres. This is the difference in litres used, not the new total
consumption. You need the original or new consumption rate to calculate either total.
Two-rate example · 7.0 and 6.5 litres/100 km over 240 km. First find the rate difference: 7.0 − 6.5
= 0.5 litres/100 km. Savings = 240 × 0.5 ÷ 100 = 1.2 litres. The original journey uses 16.8 litres and

Calculate journey consumption and
savings
Fuel arithmetic · Understand the unit. A consumption rate of 6.5 litres per 100 km means 6.5
litres for each 100 km under the supplied or measured conditions. A 200 km journey at the same
assumed rate uses twice as much, while 50 km uses half as much. Actual consumption varies
with vehicle, load, road, weather and driving. Transportstyrelsen: economical driving supplies
the driving context; the equations below are editorial arithmetic derived from the unit, not
agency-prescribed formulas.
Journey consumption: journey litres = distance in km × consumption in litres/100 km ÷ 100.
Divide distance by 100 to find the number of 100 km portions, then multiply by the supplied rate.
The kilometres cancel, leaving litres. Retain decimal working and round only the final result at
the precision requested.
Consumption example · 120 km at 6.5 litres/100 km. The journey contains 120 ÷ 100 = 1.2
portions of 100 km. Consumption = 1.2 × 6.5 = 7.8 litres. Do not multiply distance by the rate
without dividing by 100; that would misread the unit.
Savings from a supplied reduction: litres saved = distance in km × reduction in litres/100 km ÷
100. If two consumption rates are supplied, subtract the lower rate from the higher first. Multiply
that difference by the number of 100 km portions. A supplied saving is an exercise assumption,
not a guaranteed benefit of a particular driving technique.
Savings example · A reduction of 1.5 litres/100 km over 300 km. The journey has 300 ÷ 100 = 3
portions. Savings = 3 × 1.5 = 4.5 litres. This is the difference in litres used, not the new total
consumption. You need the original or new consumption rate to calculate either total.
Two-rate example · 7.0 and 6.5 litres/100 km over 240 km. First find the rate difference: 7.0 − 6.5
= 0.5 litres/100 km. Savings = 240 × 0.5 ÷ 100 = 1.2 litres. The original journey uses 16.8 litres and
the lower-rate journey 15.6 litres; their difference is also 1.2 litres. No percentage-saving promise
is implied.

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L02 · Exact values and displayed answers
Exact values and displayed answers
Precision and midpoint rounding · Keep the exact result visible. Some supplied savings
exercises display one-decimal answers without specifying precision or a rounding convention in
their prompts. Four such examples below use ties-to-even for the displayed keyed value. This
rounds to the nearest tenth; at an exact halfway value, choose the tenth whose retained digit is
even. It differs from rounding a halfway value upwards. Do not call a rounded value the exact
amount, or silently apply one convention where another is intended.
Four midpoint examples. A reduction of 0.5 litres/100 km over 150 km gives exactly 0.75 litres,
displayed as 0.8 to one decimal using ties-to-even. A reduction of 1.5 over 150 km gives exactly
2.25 litres, displayed as 2.2. A reduction of 0.5 over 250 km gives exactly 1.25 litres, displayed as
1.2. A reduction of 1.5 over 250 km gives exactly 3.75 litres, displayed as 3.8. The units for every
reduction are litres/100 km.
Compare conventions. With ordinary half-up rounding to one decimal, 2.25 becomes 2.3 and
1.25 becomes 1.3; ties-to-even gives 2.2 and 1.2. The exact products remain 2.25 and 1.25 litres.
For these supplied examples, keep the exact arithmetic and the disclosed displayed-answer
convention separate. For a new problem, follow its stated precision/convention; if they are
absent, report the exact result and recognise that a rounded answer needs an assumption.
Round once at the end, not the rate or intermediate product.
Try the fuel arithmetic. (A) Find journey consumption for 80 km at 6.5 litres/100 km. (B) Find the
saving from a supplied reduction of 0.5 litres/100 km over 250 km, first exactly and then to one
decimal using ties-to-even. (C) Find the saving over 200 km when supplied consumption falls
from 7.5 to 6.2 litres/100 km. Give your units and show the rate difference where needed.
Answers are in the separate lesson answer section.

text:
KörkortGo · M09-L03
M09-L03
Choose the journey as well as the car
Your goal: Compare combining trips, walking, cycling, public transport and driving for a
realistic personal journey.
The syllabus includes transport choices and the way personal circumstances influence them. A
useful comparison recognises that people's access needs, schedules and available services
differ. Category B syllabus, chapters 4–5
Learning approach. Start with the purpose: reaching work, collecting goods, accompanying a
person or making a visit. Then list workable options. Could two errands be combined? Could a
nearby trip be walked or cycled safely? Is public transport available for both directions? If you
share a car journey, can everyone use the required protection and travel without creating a
rushed schedule?
Do not replace one unrealistic assumption with another. A route may be short but inaccessible to
a particular person. A service may run outward but not at the return time. A car may solve those
needs, while a different choice suits the following day's journey. The exercise is to make the
choice deliberately.

M09-L04
Check where the vehicle can go
Your goal: Find official environmental-zone information and determine what to verify
before entering.
Requirements. Municipalities can introduce environmental zones under the national
framework. Class 1 concerns heavy buses and heavy goods vehicles; class 2 concerns passenger
cars and light buses/goods vehicles. For class 2, spark-ignition vehicles need Euro 5 or Euro 6 and
diesel vehicles need Euro 6. For light vehicles, class 3 ordinarily permits only electric, fuel-cell or
qualifying gas vehicles; gas vehicles must meet the specified Euro 6 emissions criteria. A light
plug-in hybrid is not admitted merely because it can sometimes run electrically. Exemptions
exist for specified vehicles and uses. Transportstyrelsen: environmental zones · Traffic
Regulation, chapter 4 §§22–24a

Independent official examples. Match an ending to the same class at the start. These signs do not assert a current
municipal boundary.

text:
KörkortGo · M10-L01
M10-L01
When the car cannot continue
Your goal: Compare a breakdown on an ordinary road, a motorway and in a tunnel.
Requirement. If a breakdown leaves a vehicle where stopping is prohibited, it must be moved to
a suitable place as soon as possible, subject to the special rules for an accident scene. Warning
obligations depend on the situation. A warning triangle must give approaching drivers enough
warning; the law does not prescribe one universal distance for every road. Traffic Regulation,
chapter 3 §§51 and 57
Official motorway/2+1-road advice. If possible, reach the safest available stopping place.
Switch on hazard lights, warn other traffic and leave the vehicle and carriageway promptly. Move
away from traffic, outside a barrier where one exists. Trafikverket recommends placing the
triangle at least 100 m away, preferably farther, and taking care while doing so, walking at the
side and outside the barrier where possible. Do not expose yourself in the traffic lane to carry out
a roadside repair. Call professional recovery; call 112 when life is in danger. Trafikverket:
breakdown advice
Tunnel advice is different. Use hazard lights, move towards the edge or an emergency bay if
possible and switch off the engine. For a non-urgent incident, Trafikverket advises staying in the
car or protected from traffic close to it while calling for assistance. In an urgent situation, leave
for the nearest emergency exit and use the assistance point, emergency phone or 112. In a fire,
leave and reach an emergency exit; follow signs, announcements and emergency personnel. Do
not turn a non-urgent-tunnel recommendation into advice to stay beside a fire. Trafikverket:
tunnels

text:
KörkortGo · M10-L01 · Overheating
Keep the hot coolant cap closed
Overheating · Leave the hot cap closed. In a conventional pressurised cooling system, hot
coolant and steam can remain under pressure even after the engine is switched off. Opening the
radiator cap, or the cap of a pressurised coolant reservoir, can release that pressure and expel
scalding liquid or steam, causing severe burns. Never loosen or remove the cap while the engine
or cooling system is hot. Switching off is not proof that pressure and heat have disappeared.
Manufacturer handbook: hot coolant and pressure warning
Treat a temperature warning as a reason to respond according to the actual vehicle handbook,
not as an invitation to open a cap. Revisit M02-L01 for warning indicators and fault recognition.
Protect people from traffic first and arrange professional assistance where needed.
Cooling-system layouts and stopping instructions vary; this lesson gives no fixed waiting time,
cap-opening sequence or roadside refill procedure. Manufacturer cooling-system precautions ·
Trafikverket: protect people and call recovery
Apply the warning. The temperature warning appears on a motorway journey. After reaching
the safest available stopping place as conditions allow, follow the vehicle's stopping instructions
and this lesson's motorway scene-safety advice. A passenger suggests opening the coolant cap
immediately because the engine is now off. Reject that action: residual heat and pressure can
still cause a burn. Call recovery from a protected position rather than attempting an exposed
repair. If the event is in a tunnel, use the tunnel response above; smoke, fire or danger to life
requires the urgent response, not waiting beside the vehicle to diagnose it. Trafikverket:
motorway breakdown · Trafikverket: tunnel urgency

text:
KörkortGo · M10-L02
M10-L02
When someone may be hurt
Your goal: Identify scene-safety, emergency-contact and first-aid learning needs following
a collision.
Requirements. If involved in a traffic accident, remain at the scene, help injured people to the
extent of your ability and assist with necessary measures. Provide your name, address and
information when requested by another involved person or someone whose property was
damaged. Notify the owner or police promptly if damaged property has nobody present to
receive the information. Notify police promptly for a personal injury that is not insignificant.
Traffic Regulation, chapter 2 §8
A vehicle creating danger or obstruction after a collision should be moved to a suitable place.
However, where someone has died or been seriously injured, move it only if it endangers other
traffic, and preserve evidence as required. Staying at the scene does not mean standing in an
active traffic lane. Protect yourself and others while arranging help. Traffic Regulation, chapter 2
§8
Emergency response. At danger to life, call 112. Give the location, direction of travel, what
happened and what dangers you can see; follow the operator's instructions. Make observations
from a safe position rather than walking into moving traffic to gather details. Trafikverket:
emergency contact

X6 · Temporary obstruction warning device
Särskild varningsanordning
A temporary obstruction restricts passage. Read the text
identifying its cause. Temporary warning device reads Olycka:
accident.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
First-aid reference. Use 1177's first-aid guidance to learn more about helping someone in an
acute situation, including when a person is unconscious or has breathing difficulties. Practical
first-aid training can help you prepare. This lesson is deliberately brief and does not reproduce
clinical procedures or a pulse-check sequence. In an emergency, call 112 rather than spending
time searching a website.
Wildlife collisions. Trafikverket advises calling 112 and marking the collision location safely so
responders can find it, even if the animal has left. Avoid approaching an injured animal. Its
guidance gives a separate precaution for wild boar, bear, lynx and wolf: continue 200 m before
stopping and marking, then call police immediately. Only move the vehicle when safe and
possible; explain the actual collision location and the animal's direction clearly. This is agency
safety guidance, not a claim that every animal species has identical statutory reporting rules.
Trafikverket: wildlife collisions

Wildlife collisions. Trafikverket advises calling 112 and marking the collision location safely so
responders can find it, even if the animal has left. Avoid approaching an injured animal. Its
guidance gives a separate precaution for wild boar, bear, lynx and wolf: continue 200 m before
stopping and marking, then call police immediately. Only move the vehicle when safe and
possible; explain the actual collision location and the animal's direction clearly. This is agency
safety guidance, not a claim that every animal species has identical statutory reporting rules.
Trafikverket: wildlife collisions

text:
KörkortGo · M10-L03
M10-L03
Explain a whole journey
Your goal: Review a mixed journey, justify decisions, identify missed hazards and propose
safer alternatives.
This exercise brings the earlier lessons together. It is an original learning scenario, not an official
test question or a court case.
Scenario. You plan to take a passenger to a rural appointment using an unfamiliar car. The
outward journey includes a residential area, a roundabout and a faster road. Rain is expected
later. At the destination, the nearest empty space is before a pedestrian crossing. On the return
journey you become delayed; the passenger asks you to pass a slower vehicle near a bend.
Work through the decisions.
1. Before leaving, establish fitness, entitlement, vehicle readiness, passenger protection and the
controls you may need. Check the route and alternatives.
2. In the residential area, identify crossings, people hidden by parked vehicles and the applicable
speed. At the roundabout, separate entry, lane and exit decisions.
3. On the faster section, preserve a following gap and a view ahead. If the weather worsens,
reassess both lighting and speed.
4. At the destination, apply the stopping restrictions before considering convenience. Choose a
lawful place with a safe manoeuvre and passenger exit.
5. On the return trip, reject an overtaking attempt without a complete clear path. Change the
arrival expectation instead of the safety margin.
The rules behind these decisions are explained in M02–M07. The duties to adapt speed, yield
where required and avoid dangerous manoeuvres remain applicable throughout. Traffic
Regulation, chapters 2–3

text:
KörkortGo · M10-L04
M10-L04
Make a realistic readiness plan
Your goal: Compare knowledge, practical performance and confidence, then plan further
learning and accessible examination preparation.
The official theory test covers vehicle knowledge/manoeuvring, environment, road safety, traffic
rules and personal factors. It checks understanding across those areas; memorising the wording
of practice questions is not equivalent preparation. The practical test requires you to apply
knowledge through vehicle checks, manoeuvres and driving in traffic. Trafikverket: category B
tests · Practical test
Current standard theory-test format, checked 1 October 2026: 70 questions, of which 65 count
towards the score; at least 52 points are needed to pass; standard time is 50 minutes. These
administrative figures can change, so verify them before booking. They are not a recommended
pass mark for this book's short learning checks. Trafikverket: theory-test format
Trafikverket provides language options, including English, and application routes for support
such as extended time, oral support or an interpreter where appropriate. Support generally
needs approval before the supported test can be booked. Check the current requirements and
apply early enough for a decision; do not assume that support can be added at the door.
Languages · Test support
Learning approach. Review three kinds of evidence: Can you explain the rule and its exceptions?
Can you recognise the situation without a prompt? Can you act safely and consistently during
supervised practice? A high confidence rating with little evidence is a learning signal, not a
readiness certificate.
Write your next practice plan in concrete terms: “Recognise cycle passages after a turn and
explain the duty before reaching them,” or “Demonstrate the safety check and explain each
defect response.” Revisit errors after a delay and in a changed scenario so that you are practising
understanding rather than recognising an answer.
Worked decision. A learner answers most checks correctly but still needs reminders to scan at
junctions. They continue targeted supervised practice instead of treating their theory score as
proof of practical readiness.

While approaching a new situation
1. Observe: What can I see, what is hidden and who might enter?
2. Identify the duty: Which rule, sign, marking, signal or authorised instruction applies?
3. Preserve space: Can I stop or alter the plan without forcing another person to avoid me?
4. Communicate: Will others understand my intended movement?
5. Recheck: Is the information still true as I begin and complete the action?
This is an original learning routine based on the observation, risk and cooperation aims of the
category B syllabus. It is not an official test sequence.
Before leaving a parked vehicle
Check that stopping and parking are permitted at that location, time and for that vehicle. Meet
fee, duration and permit conditions. Secure against rolling and unauthorised use. Check for
people before opening doors and provide a safe place for passengers to leave. See M05-L03/L04
and the Traffic Regulation, chapter 3 §§47–55.

Parkeringshus
Directs you to a parking garage. Its name may be included, and
nearby information may state whether spaces are available or
the garage is full. Check the parking conditions on arrival. The
roof above P distinguishes a garage from a general parking
destination.

accompanying symbol shows which type of transport is

train. It does not promise free parking or a free onward
journey.

A12 · Falling rocks
Varning för stenras
Falling rocks may occur, and rocks from a fall may lie on the
road. Look for debris and leave enough space to respond. This
illustration shows rocks falling from the right. The official
mirrored variant reflects conditions at the site.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-13 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/varningsmarken/varning-for-ste
nras/
A23 · Low-flying aircraft
Varning för lågt flygande flygplan
Warning of low-flying aircraft. Keep attention on the road and
be prepared for an aircraft nearby. The question illustration
points left; the official opposite-facing aircraft has the same
warning meaning.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-13 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/varningsmarken/varning-for-lagt
-flygande-flygplan/
A32 · Vehicles drawn by draught animals
Varning för fordon med förspänt dragdjur
Vehicles drawn by draught animals often cross or remain on
this road section. Look ahead for slow-moving animal-drawn
traffic and allow space. The illustration shows a horse and
cart. Official variants show other animal-drawn vehicles; the
meaning is not limited to horses.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-13 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/varningsmarken/varning-for-for
don-med-forspant-dragdjur/

text:
KörkortGo · RB17 · Country-road hazards and passing · Continued
Continue the reference
C29 · No overtaking with a heavy lorry
Förbud mot omkörning med tung lastbil
A heavy lorry must not overtake other motor-driven vehicles
except two-wheeled mopeds and two-wheeled motorcycles
without sidecars. The prohibition applies along the road until
C30 ends it. The heavy-lorry-and-car illustration restricts the
overtaking driver; it does not ban heavy-lorry access.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-13 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/forbudsmarken/forbud-mot-om
korning-med-tung-lastbil/
C30 · End of heavy-lorry overtaking prohibition
Slut på förbud mot omkörning med tung lastbil
The heavy-lorry overtaking prohibition indicated by C29 ends
here. Continue to apply the ordinary overtaking rules and
check that any manoeuvre is safe and permitted. The
crossed-out lorry-and-car symbol ends that particular
restriction; it is not an instruction to overtake.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-13 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/forbudsmarken/slut-pa-forbud-
mot-omkorning-med-tung-lastbil/

KörkortGo · RB19 · Rail crossings
RB19
Rail crossings
Warning sequence, barriers, track crossing and locating crossing identification safely.
Related lessons: M06-L04
A35 · Rail crossing with barriers
Varning för järnvägskorsning med bommar
A railway or tramway crossing fitted with barriers lies ahead.
Follow its signals and barrier indications. Barrier pictogram
inside a warning triangle.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-02 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/varningsmarken/varning-for-jar
nvagskorsning-med-bommar/
A36 · Rail crossing without barriers
Varning för järnvägskorsning utan bommar
Prepare for a railway crossing without barriers. The lack of
barriers does not mean a train cannot approach. Locomotive
inside a warning triangle.

Caption checked 2026-10-02 · English wording is editorial.

A39 · Railway crossbuck
Kryssmärke
The crossing is immediately ahead. The crossbuck
arrangement distinguishes one track from multiple tracks. A
single horizontal crossbuck, for one track.
Transportstyrelsen · official description
Caption checked 2026-10-02 · English wording is editorial.
https://www.transportstyrelsen.se/sv/vagtrafik/trafikregler-och-vagmarken/vagmarken/varningsmarken/kryssmarke/
Y1 · Flashing red rail-crossing signal
Rött blinkande ljus
Stop before the stop line or, without one, before the signal.
The red lamps flash alternately; the illustration is a still
representation. Two red signal lamps and a lower lamp within
a downward-pointing signal backing; red flashing is
represented by a still drawing.
Transportstyrelsen · official description

Y2 · Rail-crossing audible warning
Ljudsignal
Do not enter the crossing while the audible warning is
sounding. This graphic is only a sound icon, not a recording or
a flashing-light instruction. Grey speaker icon with sound
waves; no audio is supplied.
